description:
The Spirit of 2010 Trail is a series of historic rail lines that pass through many communities across southern BC from the Fraser Canyon and Brookmere to Slocan Lake. The trail is comprised of the Kettle Valley Rail Trail, Columbia & Western Rail Trail and Slocan Rail Trail.

For a comfortable and enjoyable ride, a gravel bike or a mountain bike with wider tires is recommended. While some sections are relatively smooth, others feature loose gravel, sand, and washboard surfaces. The trail has also seen impacts in recent years due to major flooding events and aging infrastructure. Review closure notes below.
Public Notice:

See attached KVR Trail Updates document for recent information regarding hazards, closures and detours.

The maintenance of the trail is supported by the Regional District of the Okanagan Similkameen and the Trails to the Boundary Society. Both have active facebook pages with updated trail information.

Due to the Bald Range Fire near Summerland, the KVR is closed from ~2km east of Osprey Lake Recreation Site (at the junction with the Princeton-Summerland Road) to Summerland. Please do not use this section while Wildfire Services is actively working to combat the fire in the area.

This trail is for recreational users only. Bridge weight limits are unknown - use at your own risk. Equestrian riders must dismount to cross unless expressly prohibited.

The Kettle Valley Rail Trail will be closed at 93km (approximately 25km North of Beaverdell). Use posted detour.

Due to impacts of flooding, the 67km section of the KVRT from Princeton to Brodie Siding (Coquihalla Highway) is closed to ALL traffic.
directions: Access to the trail is possible from the many communities that the rail trail passes through. There are many access points where the trail crosses industry logging roads. Be mindfull of those sections of the trail with both motorized and non motorized use.
